artifacts.summary: Locates the skip site and the second silent-exit site in literature-briefing.sh, confirms literature-lit-flag-resolve.sh is out of scope, and recommends folding a new skip-rate signal into the existing sparse marker/banner machinery so both existing consumers respond with zero changes to either flow file.

memory_candidates.content: In the literature extension's lit-coverage marker family (UNVERIFIED/DEGRADED RETRIEVAL/SPARSE COVERAGE banners), when adding a new failure signal, prefer folding it into an EXISTING boolean/marker that downstream code already greps for (e.g. `sparse=true`) rather than inventing a new marker field nothing consumes. A signal nobody reads is still silent, and reusing an existing consumed flag satisfies both 'must fire' and 'existing consumers must keep working unchanged' acceptance criteria simultaneously.

literature-lit-flag-resolve.sh (Stage 4a Checkpoint 1, pre-generation) deliberately does NOT cross-reference sub-index doc_ids against the global index, per its own header comment citing 'Risk 4: counting duplication'. Any task about doc_id resolution failure/coverage accuracy in the literature extension belongs entirely in literature-briefing.sh (Checkpoint 2, post-generation), not in the resolver script.
